height.location: NOT PUBLISHED - sentinel 0; see not_found. Only published size constraint is the ~250 mm specimen length that the test space must accommodate.
height.quote: systems that can accommodate tensile specimens up to approximately 250 mm long under controlled cryogenic conditions.

width_or_diameter.location: NOT PUBLISHED - sentinel 0; see not_found. NPL's requirements report only states the dewar is ~20-25 litres and must fit between the test-machine columns.
width_or_diameter.quote: The volume of the cryostat test dewar for mechanical testing is approximately 20-25 litres.

outer.color_note: No photograph or colour specification published. Requirements report (MAT 102) describes a double-wall vessel: outer-jacketed LN2 dewar surrounding an inner LHe dewar, mounted on a T-slotted platen of a servo-hydraulic load frame with top-mounted actuator.

stages.name: Test dewar / wet bath (specimen, grips and pull-rods submerged in controllably boiling liquid helium, heater-regulated to 20 K)
stages.quote: for 20 K, a novel temperature control configuration was developed, operating on the principal of controllably boiling liquid helium inside the test dewar with a set of heating elements.

sample_space.description: Flat rectangular composite coupon (or metallic flat/cylindrical specimen) held between pull-rod-mounted cryogenic grips inside a wet-bath test dewar; at 20 K the test space is filled with liquid helium boiled controllably by heater elements. The dewar must accommodate specimens of approximately 250 mm length; the NPL grip-validation coupons were 250 mm x 25 mm x 5 mm.
sample_space.shape: cylindrical dewar bath around a flat coupon load train

height.location: maximum tensile specimen length accommodated in the test space (not the dewar depth)
height.quote: systems that can accommodate tensile specimens up to approximately 250 mm long under controlled cryogenic conditions.

diameter_or_width.location: width of the standard coupon tested in NPL's cryogenic grips (dewar inner diameter not published)
diameter_or_width.quote: specimens were straight rectangular coupons (dimensions of 250 mm x 25 mm x 5 mm) and were gripped without additional end-tabs.

wiring.to: one on each grip and one on the specimen
wiring.quote: Three Type-T thermocouples were used to measure temperature during the test, one mounted on each grip and one in direct contact with the specimen.

wiring.to: heating elements in the liquid-helium test dewar (count not published)
wiring.quote: controllably boiling liquid helium inside the test dewar with a set of heating elements.

windows.quote: The dewar should feature inlet and outlet ports in the top flange (Figure 4, C), a suitable cryogen dispenser mechanism and sensors to control and monitor temperature

moving_parts.quote: Specimens were loaded in displacement control at 2 mm/min until failure.
moving_parts.rate: 2 mm/min crosshead/actuator displacement (pull-rod load train, top-mounted servo-hydraulic actuator)

moving_parts.quote: operating on the principal of controllably boiling liquid helium inside the test dewar with a set of heating elements.
moving_parts.rate: helium boil-off vapour from heater-regulated bath; rate not published

not_found: load frame / cryostat load rating as built (MAT 102 specifies a 250 kN requirement; grip paper gives 100 or 250 kN grip rating and 60 kN preload, none stated as the 20 K rig's rating)
notes: Bespoke NPL facility, not a catalogue product. Sources: (1) NPL cryogenic testing services page: helium cooling with active temperature control for ~20 K, capabilities to 4 K, 'bespoke LN2 and LHe cryostats', specimens up to ~250 mm. (2) CEC/ICMC 2025 abstract M4Or1B-02 (Spetsieris, Gower, Giannis, NPL): wet-bath cryostat; 77 K by submerging the rig in LN2, 20 K by controllably boiling LHe in the test dewar with heating elements. (3) ECCM21 2024 grip paper (eprintspublications.npl.co.uk/10069): cylindrical cryogenic grips rated 100 or 250 kN, steel pull-rods, 60 kN preload, 250x25x5 mm coupons, three Type-T thermocouples, 2 mm/min displacement control, 'liquid flow cryostat' submerged in LN2 at 77 K. (4) NPL Report MAT 102 (2022) is a REQUIREMENTS specification for the planned system, not an as-built description: servo-hydraulic frame with top-mounted actuator, 250 kN load cell, telescopic lift cylinders for the dewar top, T-slotted platen, ~20-25 litre double-wall dewar (LN2 jacket around LHe inner), top-flange inlet/outlet ports, thermal baffles, 20-300 K control with ±2 K accuracy; use these only as 'design intent'. Rendering guidance: vertical dewar on a load-frame base, pull-rod from a top actuator, coupon in bath; LHe liquid plus heater-driven bubbling/vapour at 20 K. Lean temperature capability for this configuration is the single 20 K point (20000 mK), consistent with the NPL page. 'probe_arm' is used for the moving pull-rod/actuator since no tensile-specific enum exists.
